In this position you will serve as a first line supervisor over a team of Program Managers who are engaged in managing critical program segments for which the scope and effect of the work have an Office of Field Operations-wide impact.

You will oversee a variety of law enforcement programs, to include enforcement operations for drug interdiction and seized narcotics accountability. This position starts at a salary of $143,913.00 (GS-14, Step 1) to $187,093.00 (GS-14, Step 10).

Typical duties include: Planning, organizing, coordinating, controlling, and evaluating the activities of an organization(s) Overseeing the overall planning, direction, and timely execution of a program or several program segments, each of which is managed through separate subordinate organizational units Leading complex projects, often cutting across organizational/activity lines, defining critical quality factors and process improvements Assuring implementation by subordinate organizations and operating units of the goals and objectives of a CBP-wide program Determining goals and objectives that need additional emphasis; developing measures that evaluate performance; making recommendations for program improvement; and managing all resources as corporate assets GS Salary: Visit this link to view the locality pay tables by geographic area.

If you do not see your geographic area listed, select the "Rest of United States" pay table. Some positions fall under a special pay rate depending on the series, grade level and location of the position. Please visit this link to view special pay rate charts.
Experience: You qualify for the GS-14 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Planning, directing, and evaluating major program segments that include diverse professional, technical, and administrative activities, with impact across a headquarters-level office or nationwide program, including development and execution of multi-year work plans and goals.

Leading complex, cross-organizational projects as a subject matter expert, including applying analytical methodologies (such as statistical tools, mathematical techniques, and process mapping) to improve service delivery, reduce costs, increase quality, and develop and justify business cases.

Providing technical direction in project management, team building, facilitation, process improvement analysis, and the methodology required to develop and substantiate a business case for the selected project.

Overseeing law enforcement-related programs such as inspection, intelligence analysis, drug interdiction, and seized property accountability, including ensuring enforcement of applicable laws and policies, overseeing enforcement actions, and ensuring proper custody, preservation, and disposition of contraband and seized property.

Managing organizational change and resources, including approving allocation and distribution of funds, implementing internal controls in accordance with the Federal Managers' Integrity Act, identifying and resolving issues where no policy exists, and coordinating with senior officials within and outside the agency to address complex, cross-cutting program issues.

NOTE: Your resume must explicitly indicate how you meet this requirement, otherwise you will be found ineligible. Please see the "Required Documents" section below for additional resume requirements.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

You must: Meet all qualification requirements, including education if applicable to this position, subject to verification at any stage of the application process; and Meet all applicable Time in Grade requirements (current federal employees must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade or equivalent grade band in the federal service) by 08/12/2026.

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees.

If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Background Investigation: U.S.

Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is a federal law enforcement agency that requires all applicants to undergo a thorough background investigation prior to employment in order to promote the agency's core values of vigilance, service to country, and integrity.

During the screening and/or background investigation process, you will be asked questions regarding any felony criminal convictions or current felony charges, the use of illegal drugs (e.g., marijuana, cocaine, heroin, LSD, methamphetamines, ecstasy), and the use of non-prescribed controlled substances including any experimentation, possession, sale, receipt, manufacture, cultivation, production, transfer, shipping, trafficking, or distribution of controlled substances.

For additional information on the preemployment process, review the following link: Applicant Resources | CBP Careers Residency: There is a residency requirement for all applicants not currently employed by CBP.

Individuals are required to have physically resided in the United States or its protectorates (as declared under international law) for at least three of the last five years.

If you do not meet the residency requirement and you have been physically located in a foreign location for more than two of the last five years, you may request an exception to determine if you are eligible for a residency waiver by meeting one or more of the following conditions: Working for the U.S.

Government as a federal civilian or as a member of the military A dependent who was authorized to accompany a federal civilian or member of the military who was working for the U.S. government Participation in a study abroad program sponsored by a U.S. affiliated college or university Working as a contractor, intern, consultant or volunteer supporting the U.S. government Probationary Period: All employees new to the federal government must serve a one year probationary period during the first year of his/her initial permanent federal appointment to determine fitness for continued employment.

Current and former federal employees may be required to serve or complete a probationary period. Agency Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP) Eligibles: If you have never worked for the federal government, you are not CTAP eligible. View information about CTAP eligibility on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.

You must submit the supporting documents listed under the Required Documents section of this announcement.

The purpose of the Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI) Program Manager is to provide independent clinical administration of the Primary Care Mental Health program and supervision of interdisciplinary staff who work in the Program.

Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional Duties include, but are not limited to: The incumbent carries out the following supervisory authorities and responsibilities: Provides direct line supervision of an interdisciplinary team of PCMHI staff, including social workers, psychologists, and prescribing providers, with anticipation of program expansion.

Plans work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares schedules for completion of work. Assigns work to subordinates based on priorities, selective consideration of the difficulty and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees. Evaluates work performance of subordinates.

Coordinating services offered to veterans and their families enrolled in the program. Services include functional assessment, medications, crisis intervention, educational, individual, and group treatment, interventions specific to chronic health conditions, and care management.

Formulating, interpreting, and implementing policies and procedures pertaining to quality mental health care in PCMHI to assure compliance with internal and external performance standards. Developing effective programs and treatment strategies for PCMHI program patients.

Interfacing with other program Managers, Service Chief, Mental Health product line leadership, and VA personnel. Advising Mental Health leadership on relevant programmatic issues with recommendations for improvement in service delivery. Collaborating with other program directors and managers as a member of the Mental Health Executive Committee.

Collaborating with Primary Care executive staff as a member of the PACT Steering Committee. Maintaining effective working relationship with internal and external customer groups. Adhering to the requirements of the Master Agreement between the Department of Veterans Affairs and the American Federation of Government Employees.

The program manager will provide PCMHI-consistent care to patients within the PCMHI clinic.

This may include engaging patients through alternative technologies (e.g., telehealth, CVT to home) Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 8:00am-4:30pm (subject to change based on facility needs) Recruitment Incentive (Sign-on Bonus): Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (Relocation Assistance): Not Authorized EDRP Authorized: Former EDRP participants ineligible to apply for incentive.

Contact raja.kadeem@va.gov, the EDRP Coordinator for questions/assistance. Learn more Pay: Competitive salary and regular salary increases. When setting pay, a higher step rate of the appropriate grade may be determined after consideration of higher or unique qualifications or special needs of the VA (Above Minimum Rate of the Grade).

Paid Time Off: 37-50 days of annual paid time offer per year (13-26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year)Selected applicants may qualify for credit toward annual leave accrual, based on prior work experience or military service experience.

Parental Leave: After 12 months of employment, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave in connection with the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child.

Child Care Subsidy: After 60 days of employment, full time employees with a total family income below $144,000 may be eligible for a childcare subsidy up to 25% of total eligible childcare costs for eligible children up to the monthly maximum of $416.66.

Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met. Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship. Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education. Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed. For the purpose of meeting this requirement, the term "specialty area" refers to the specific specialty areas recognized by the accrediting body and not to specific job duties that might require special skills.

Currently, APA accredits doctoral programs in the specialty areas of clinical psychology, counseling psychology, school psychology, or combinations of two or more of those areas. PCSAS accredits doctoral programs in psychological clinical science.

CPA accredits doctoral programs in clinical psychology, counseling psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and school psychology. There are no job assignments in VHA that require the skills of a school psychologist; therefore, an applicant with a degree in the specialty area of school psychology is not eligible for appointment.

Strictly for the purpose of determining eligibility for appointment as a psychologist in VHA, there is no distinction between the specialty areas (with the exception of school psychology).

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re- specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re- specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: (a) The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and, (b) the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature. AND Internships.

Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96- 151 (pre- 1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally- accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one- year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program. Licensure.

Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria). Grade Determinations: Psychology Program Manager, GS-14 Experience.

At least three years of experience as a professional psychologist, with at least one year equivalent to the GS-13 grade level. Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities.

In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate all of the following KSAs: Ability to organize work, set priorities, delegate tasks, and meet multiple deadlines. Knowledge of and ability to utilize evidence based practices and clinical practice guidelines appropriately and ability to guide staff in using these tools.

Ability to deal effectively with individuals or groups. Skill in managing and directing the work of others to accomplish program goals and objectives. Ability to translate management goals and objectives into well-coordinated and controlled work operations. Ability to establish and monitor production and performance priorities and standards.

Ability to analyze organizational and operational problems and to develop and implement solutions that result in sound operation of the program. Preferred Experience: PCMHI experience, supervisory experience. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-14. Physical Requirements: Physical aspects associated with work required of this assignment are typical for the occupation, see Duties section for essential job duties of the position. May require standing, lifting, carrying, sitting, stooping, bending, puling, and pushing.

May be required to wear personal protective equipment and undergo annual TB screening or testing as conditions of employment. Work Environment: Work is performed in an office/clinic setting with minimal risks that requires normal safety precautions; the area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated.

However, the work environment requires someone with the ability to handle several tasks at once in sometimes stressful situations.

Hi, I'm Jace , and I founded Ashby's Customer Education function in 2025. We've expanded the team since then, I now lead the team and am excited to be hiring our next Program Manager!
Our team is built on a simple belief: Ashby Academy should feel like every customer's personal CSM. Regardless of tier or team size, every Ashby customer deserves content that meets them where they are — practical, accurate, and genuinely useful.

That standard shapes everything we build, and it's what's driven the development of our growing Academy courses, webinar program, and playbook library. We have ambitions to expand both the depth of our content and the formats we deliver it in, and this hire is a meaningful part of getting there.
As our next Customer Education Program Manager, you'll own customer-facing education work end to end. We're looking for someone who knows Ashby well enough to coach users on how to use it, and can translate that coaching into content that scales. You'll turn complex product workflows into clear, practical learning experiences, and partner closely with Customer Success, Product, PMM, and Recruiting Operations Consulting to make sure what we build is grounded in how customers actually work.
This is a hands-on role. You won't be setting strategy and handing it off. You'll be in the work: scoping, writing, building, reviewing, refining, and shipping.

Own net-new customer education work from concept through publication, including courses, playbooks, recordings, and other learning assets
Define the goal and shape of each learning asset — what it should help customers do, for whom, and in what format — then gather SME input, design the approach, and build it
Refresh and improve existing Academy content so it stays aligned with how Ashby actually works today
Translate complex Ashby workflows into clear, practical, outcome-oriented education — the kind that helps customers understand not just what to do, but why it matters
Partner cross-functionally with CS, Product, PMM, and RecOps Consultants to identify high-value education opportunities and get the right assets out at the right time
Contribute to the systems, standards, and workflows that help Customer Education scale while maintaining high-quality learning experiences
Help us explore adjacent formats when useful — lighter-weight tutorials, in-app guidance, and other just-in-time learning moments
Typical workload: You'll manage 2-3 new courses or major playbooks per quarter, plus ongoing refreshes and maintenance of existing content. Most of your time goes into building the work yourself (writing, recording, designing learning flows).
Examples of work you might own
Build a new Academy course that helps customers adopt a new Ashby feature or module
Turn product and SME input into a practical playbook tied to a real recruiting outcome
Record voiceover for a customer-facing learning asset
Audit and refresh an existing course after a product change so it reflects how Ashby works today
Partner with RecOps Consulting or other SMEs to build something that helps customers apply a concept, not just understand it
Experiment with lighter-weight format when a full course isn't the right answer

You already know Ashby well. You understand how its workflows are structured, where users can get stuck, and what it takes to use it effectively. Formal customer education experience isn't required. What matters is Ashby fluency and the ability to translate that into coaching and content.
Beyond your Ashby depth, you could be a great fit if you also have:
You've taught something complex before. Whether live, through writing, or both, you've helped someone understand a complicated product or process and have ideas on how to turn that into something scalable.
You can juggle multiple projects. You manage several at once without losing momentum when priorities shift.
You're a strong writer. You can make complicated things feel clear and useful on the page.
You're comfortable recording voiceovers. Recording yourself for customer-facing content feels natural, not like a stretch.
You own work end-to-end. You can take something from problem framing through build and launch without needing a fully mapped plan first.
You work well with subject matter experts. You know how to pull what you need from busy stakeholders without losing momentum or clarity.
You have good judgment about scope. You can tell when something should be deep, lightweight, or optimized for speed, and you choose intentionally.
Traditional customer education experience isn't required. The background that matters most is hands-on Ashby experience — as a recruiter, a recruiting ops practitioner, an implementation specialist, a CSM, or someone who has simply used Ashby deeply enough to teach it. If you've owned meaningful work with real autonomy, improved how something gets taught or documented, and cared about outcomes over optics, you'll likely feel at home here.
This role may not be a fit if
You're still building Ashby fluency. This role leans on already knowing Ashby well, since you'll be teaching it from day one. If you haven't had the chance to build that hands-on depth yet, this particular role isn't the right fit.
You prefer to set strategy and hand it off. This is a hands-on role. You'll be the one scoping, writing, recording, and shipping, not directing someone else to do it.
You need a fully defined scope before you can do your best work. You'll often be the one deciding what shape an asset takes and how deep to take it, without a fully mapped plan.
You'd rather optimize an established system than help shape one. You'll have the chance to define how this program works and put your stamp on the approach, building something you're proud of rather than fine-tuning what's already set.
You want a coordination or project-management role. This is a maker seat. Most of your time goes into building the work yourself, not managing a queue of other people's.
You measure success by how much content ships. We care about whether the right education gets built and whether customers actually use it: engagement, progress, adoption of the workflows it supports, and reduced dependence on 1:1 support are all signs that the work is landing.
You're energized by large, highly structured teams. You'll often be responsible for identifying where structure is needed and putting it in place yourself
About Ashby
We’re building the next generation of enterprise software and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We are well-funded, have incredible product market fit, and are backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom
We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, over 4,000 customers, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet, but you now probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role

Mindpeak is building cutting-edge AI technology to transform cancer diagnostics for the better. Our AI-powered software is already in clinical use across more than 25 countries, helping pathologists assess tumour tissue faster, more accurately, and more consistently. Every year, tens of thousands of cancer patients already benefit from quicker and more accurate diagnoses enabled by our technology.
Our mission is to scale this impact worldwide and help make personalised, effective cancer treatment accessible to every patient no matter where they are. By combining state-of-the-art AI with real-world clinical impact, we’re working toward a future where every cancer patient gets the best possible diagnosis and, ultimately, the best possible care.

Every new laboratory that implements our AI for routine diagnostics is a project with a lot of moving parts. The software is connected to the laboratory's image management and information systems, our AI is validated on their cases, pathologists are trained, and the requirements of their market and accreditors are met.

Each of these projects brings together laboratory directors, pathologists and IT teams on the customer side, scanner and software partners, and our product, ML, engineering and quality teams internally.
As Clinical Implementation Manager you lead those projects. You own the plan, direct the specialists who do the technical work, and carry the go-live date. Once a laboratory is live you stay with them as their main contact, owning support and our long-term success with the partner. This is not a sales role and you do not carry a sales target.
What you'll own
Onboarding projects
Build and own the project plan for each new laboratory, from kickoff to go-live, with dependencies and dates kept current.
Direct the work across our product, ML, engineering and quality teams and the customer's staff.
Accompany the validations customers run as part of onboarding. The laboratory's medical director designs the study; you make sure the technical setup is correctly installed and working, that our teams deliver what the validation depends on, and that the customer has everything they need to complete it.
Carry the committed go-live date, and raise risks early with options rather than after a slip.
Customer success after go-live
Act as the customer's main point of contact once live, monitoring usage and engagement and reaching out proactively.
Own incoming support requests: resolve what you can, coordinate product and engineering on the rest, and close the loop with the customer.
Bring what you learn from customers into product planning, and flag potential expansion opportunities to Sales where relevant.Bring what you learn from customers into product planning.
You do not carry a sales target. But flagging expansion opportunities to Sales is part of your responsibility.
How you'll start
You will take on real customer onboarding projects from the start and lead them yourself, with close support from the team and from your manager in the beginning. As you build familiarity with our products and our customers, you move into running them independently.
Your Profile
A degree in biology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, medicine, or a related field.
3+ years leading projects with external customers — clinical or diagnostic implementation, digital pathology, medical device or laboratory rollout, health IT deployment, or comparable delivery work.
Proven ability to build a realistic project plan and drive it to a date, updating it responsibly and transparently as things change.
Proven ability to direct people inside and outside the company.
Technically confident: able to discuss interfaces, integrations and data credibly with ML engineers and IT staff, instruct them clearly, and translate between them and the customer.
Able to hold a room with a laboratory director, a pathologist and an IT lead, and keep all three aligned.
Full professional proficiency in English. German is not required.
Based in Hamburg, or willing to relocate, and working on-site with the team.
Willing to travel to customer sites internationally — occasional trips, typically a few times a year, focus on US customers.
Comfortable with the occasional late-afternoon or early-evening call to overlap with customers in other time zones.

Experience in pathology, diagnostics or laboratory environments, or a background in the natural sciences.
If you have not worked in pathology: evidence that you have become competent in an unfamiliar technical domain before.
Experience working within a quality management system, or delivering software into a regulated clinical setting.
Commercial instinct.
Why Mindpeak
Our vision is personalized, effective cancer treatment for every patient.
Build foundational AI systems that power both clinical cancer diagnostics and data-driven drug development, and actively shape the future of personalized medicine.
An open, creative environment with flat hierarchies and fast decisions.
A leadership team that invests in continuous development.

The incumbent reports to and collaborates with the GMH/BHIP Program Manager to ensure effective functioning of all BHIP operations. Responsibilities include helping develop and implement policies and procedures; supervising BHIP staff; establishing goals and objectives; and monitoring, evaluating, and coordinating BHIP services.

Duties encompass strategic planning, resource deployment, performance and quality improvement, and promoting recovery oriented, team-based care. The BHIP Supervisory Psychiatrist works with other BHIP supervisors to ensure compliance with VHA directives, Joint Commission standards, State licensure requirements, and VAOIG expectations.

They conduct ongoing reviews and evaluations to ensure adherence to regulatory and accreditation standards. A portion of the incumbent's time is dedicated to direct clinical service.

Establishes guidelines and performance expectations for the staff supervised, which are clearly communicated through the formal employee performance management system; Establishes and monitors productivity targets for staff supervised; Observes employee performance and conducts work performance critiques in accordance with performance expectations, which included FPPEs and OPPEs; Establishes and monitors clinic profiles in terms of availability, utilization and scheduling, and staff productivity; Monitors and reports data from relevant BHIP and provider management dashboards, as indicated; Provides informal feedback and periodically evaluates employee performance formally; Coordinates performance evaluations with Discipline Leads for direct reports who are outside of Psychiatry; Resolves informal complaints and grievances; develops work improvement plans, recommending personnel actions as indicated; Exercises supervisory authorities and responsibilities involving work assignment; Reviews the administrative and personnel management functions relative to the staff supervised; Assists with performance measure monitoring, evaluation and action plans for enhancement as well as accreditation reviews and pertinent site visits; Guides and oversees BHIP services and delivery of services, determining staffing requirements and assignments in conjunction with members of treatment teams and staff areas where individual skills are best utilized; Incumbent assists with directing operation and management of key clinical, training, and administrative programs of the team; Remedying actions: Resolves informal complaints and grievances; Establishes and executes performance improvement plans; Makes personnel recommendations; Enforces disciplinary measures as appropriate to delegated authority and in coordination with Human Resource Management Service (HRMS) and appropriate Union representatives; Incumbent hears and resolves complaints voiced by BHIP staff and works to resolve issues involving direct reports and other team members on the BHIP team; and Incumbent is responsible for furthering the goals of equal employment opportunity (EEO) by taking positive steps to assure the accomplishment of affirmative action objectives and by adhering to nondiscriminatory employment practices in regard to race, color, religion, sex, and affirmative action for the area under incumbent supervision Operational duties: Reviews and approves or disapproves leave requests; Assures that direct reports are trained and fully comply with the provisions of the safety regulations as appropriate for general and area specific operations; Reviewing and assuring that the documentation of the assigned staff reflects the services provided and meets TJC, Health Care System, and mental health documentation standards; Works with local medical center, health care center or community-based outpatient clinic leadership to meet site specific administrative and operational goals and may assume local leadership functions as necessary and as approved by BHIP Program Manager, Lead Psychiatrist, or the ACOS MH; and Works with BHIP Program Manager and Discipline Leads in identifying and prioritizing BHIP resource needs to include staffing and equipment needs of BHIP providers.

Duties related to the area of mentoring: Provides work related advice and counsel to employees with purposes of further developing careers of subordinates, as deemed appropriate by incumbent and in line with employees' clinical disciplines and practice areas.

Clinical guidance: Coordinates and monitors clinical training/development of direct reports who provide psychotherapy, mental health assessments, care management, and other psychosocial services; Responsible for assessing, verifying, monitoring, and reporting on the clinical competency of supervisees providing these services, and Considers and recommends staff members for further clinical training and development based on staff abilities, goals, and clinic operational needs.

*Die Direktion Pflege unterstützt die Führungsverantwortlichen der Pflege mit übergeordneten Dienstleistungen bei der Sicherstellung des operativen Betriebs. Dazu gehören der Personalpool qualifizierte Pflege, der Personalpool Sitzwachen und Pflegeassistenz sowie das Zentrale Bettenmanagement (ZBM).
Als Abteilungsleiter:in Ressourcenmanagement Pflege verantworten Sie diese Dienstleistungen und entwickeln sie gemeinsam mit den Führungsverantwortlichen der Pflege weiter. Gleichzeitig gestalten Sie die Zusammenarbeit mit dem künftigen Integralen Kapazitätenmanagement (IKM) mit.*
## **Das erwartet Sie** ##
* Sie führen die Abteilung Ressourcenmanagement Pflege mit den Personalpools und dem Zentralen Bettenmanagement
* Sie stellen den zuverlässigen operativen Betrieb und die bedarfsgerechte Bereitstellung der Dienstleistungen sicher
* Sie führen und entwickeln die Ihnen unterstellten Führungspersonen und Mitarbeitenden
* Sie arbeiten eng mit den Führungsverantwortlichen der Pflege zusammen, nehmen deren Bedürfnisse auf und entwickeln die Angebote entsprechend weiter
* Sie nutzen Daten und Kennzahlen, um die Dienstleistungen bedarfsgerecht und wirtschaftlich zu steuern
* Sie überprüfen und entwickeln Prozesse und Schnittstellen im Ressourcenmanagement weiter
* Sie gestalten die Zusammenarbeit mit dem künftigen Integralen Kapazitätenmanagement mit
* Sie wirken bei übergeordneten Projekten und Entwicklungen im Ressourcen- und Kapazitätsmanagement mit
## **Das bringen Sie mit** ##
* Sie verfügen über eine Ausbildung als dipl. Pflegefachfrau:mann HF oder einen Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BScN)
* Sie verfügen über eine Weiterbildung auf Masterstufe (MSc, MA, MAS) in Betriebswirtschaft, Gesundheitsökonomie, Healthcare Management oder eine gleichwertige Weiterbildung
* Sie bringen mehrjährige klinische Berufserfahrung in der Pflege sowie Führungserfahrung mit
* Sie kennen die Anforderungen und Abläufe des pflegerischen Kerngeschäfts und haben ein gutes Verständnis für betriebliche Zusammenhänge
* Sie denken und handeln dienstleistungsorientiert und arbeiten gerne mit unterschiedlichen Führungspersonen und Bereichen zusammen
* Sie verfügen über eine hohe Affinität zu Daten und Kennzahlen und verbinden analytisches mit betriebswirtschaftlichem Denken
* Sie arbeiten strukturiert, handeln lösungsorientiert und behalten auch in einem dynamischen Umfeld den Überblick
## **Unser Angebot** ##
* In dieser Funktion übernehmen Sie die Verantwortung für zentrale Dienstleistungen
* Sie unterstützen damit die Führungsverantwortlichen der Pflege im operativen Alltag
* Sie erhalten die Möglichkeit, das Ressourcenmanagement Pflege gemeinsam mit der Pflegelinie weiterzuentwickeln
* Sie gestalten die Zusammenarbeit mit dem künftigen Integralen Kapazitätenmanagement mit
* Es erwartet Sie eine vielseitige Führungsaufgabe mit Gestaltungsspielraum und einem breiten Netzwerk innerhalb der Insel Gruppe

s.h: **REJOIGNEZ L-ÉQUIPE DE L-ORÉAL LUXE ET DE LANCÔME**
s.t:
Es-tu passionné(e) par la beauté et la joie de vivre ? Crois-tu au pouvoir du bonheur pour révéler la beauté de chaque individu ?
Depuis 1935, Lancôme croit que le bonheur est la plus grande source de beauté. Depuis 90 ans, Lancôme s'attache à faire rayonner les femmes du monde entier, aussi heureuses et belles qu'elles le sont vraiment. 90 ans de générosité, d'authenticité et d'excellence, au service de toutes les femmes. Au-delà de résultats experts, découvrez chez Lancôme la joie de vivre d'une véritable innovation, source d'inspiration, de personnalisation et d'élégance à la française.
Nous offrons des parcours de carrière passionnants : développe tes compétences et ta passion dans un environnement de luxe et explore divers parcours au sein de Lancôme Beauty et de L'Oréal. Parmi ces opportunités, tu pourras évoluer vers différents rôles tels que Make up Expert, Skin care Expert, Perfume Specialist, Brand sell out coach, etc. Bénéficie de programmes de formation exclusifs Giorgio Armani Beauty, ainsi que d'un accès aux nombreuses opportunités d'apprentissage de L'Oréal.

Présent sur 150 marchés et 5 continents, L-Oréal se consacre depuis plus d'un siècle à "créer la beauté qui fait bouger le monde". Avec un chiffre d'affaires consolidé de 42 milliards d'euros, le groupe est aujourd'hui leader mondial de l'industrie cosmétique. Ensemble, nous relevons des défis complexes à grande échelle, tout en nous engageant à rendre le monde plus inclusif et plus durable, pour tous et pour la planète.
L-Oréal Luxe, leader mondial de la beauté de luxe et des parfums haut de gamme, compte plus de 35 000 expert(e)s beauté à travers le monde. Notre mission est de créer les meilleurs produits et expériences de beauté de luxe en parfumerie, soin et maquillage. À travers un portefeuille de 25 marques prestigieuses et complémentaires, L-Oréal Luxe exprime sa vision unique de la beauté de luxe : La Culture de l-Écart.
*Nous nous engageons à garantir des processus de recrutement inclusifs et à promouvoir l'embauche et la promotion de chaque candidat(e) de manière éthique et équitable.*

The Associate Project Manager is a generalist member of the PMO supporting a large federal facilities program delivered across multiple sites and task orders.

You will work across PMO functions, including schedule, risk, change control, reporting, and deliverable review, and you will be deployed where the program needs support most, including site level work and phase gate reviews.

You will operate with oversight from the PMO Director and senior project managers and may lead smaller scopes independently as you build experience.
This is a remote role on Eastern Time with travel to program sites as required. Candidates must be US citizens able to obtain a public trust and security clearance.

· Support senior project managers across active task orders with planning, scheduling, procurement coordination, quality, and risk from initiation through closeout.
· Maintain site level risk registers and change control logs, confirm every entry has an owner and a mitigation, and prepare inputs for weekly program risk reviews.
· Track progress against approved baselines, report status and variances, and draft corrective action plans for review.
· Support deliverable reviews and phase gate checkpoints, including coordinating technical reviewers, tracking comments to closure, and confirming deliverables meet contract requirements before submission to the client.
· Prepare and maintain project documentation in accordance with program governance and client requirements, and support the transition of project data into the program's systems, including Power BI and Kahua.
· Identify work requested outside current contract scope and route it through the change control process.
· Step into a needs package or site team on short notice to cover gaps, coordinate with field staff, and report back to the PMO.
· Coordinate with client and partner counterparts to keep submissions, approvals, and reporting aligned.
· Model behaviors consistent with CBRE RISE values. Other duties as assigned.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent related experience.
Two or more years supporting projects in a federal, infrastructure, facilities, or construction environment. Experience on a federal program with multiple task orders is strongly preferred.
Working knowledge of schedule, risk, and change control fundamentals and the ability to apply them without detailed direction.
Ability to read technical drawings and specifications well enough to support deliverable and site reviews.
Strong written communication, with the ability to turn field and technical information into clear status for leadership.
Comfort working across organizational boundaries with client, partner, and subcontractor staff.
Ability to travel to program sites

CAPM or PMP.
Experience with Power BI, Kahua, or similar project information systems.
Prior exposure to FAA, DoD, or other federal facilities programs.
Familiarity with earned value or level of effort contract tracking.

We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.
When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.
Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.
We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day.

As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

## Fachbereichsleiter / Fachbereichsleiterin Sozialberatung ##
Das Zentrum für Soziales ist einer der grössten Verbände seiner Art in der Schweiz.

Im Auftrag von 28 Gemeinden mit einem Einzugsgebiet von über 100'000 Personen sind wir mit grossem Engagement, niederschwellig und vernetzt in folgenden Bereichen tätig: Kindes- und Erwachsenenschutzbehörde (KESB), Berufsbeistandschaft, Sozialberatung, Mütter- und Väterberatung, Suchtberatung und Schulsozialarbeit.

Der Fachbereich Sozial- und Suchtberatung ist polyvalent tätig und bietet eine breite Palette an Beratungsangeboten an. Dazu gehören persönliche und wirtschaftliche Sozialhilfe, Jugend- und Erziehungsberatung, Budget- und Schuldenberatung, Abklärungen für Gemeinden und im Bereich des Kindesschutzes für die KESB sowie Suchtberatungen.

Zum Fachbereich gehört auch die Schulsozialarbeit in elf Gemeinden.
Da die bisherige Stelleninhaberin aus familiären Gründen in ihre ursprüngliche Wohnregion zurückkehrt, ist die Stelle per Dezember 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung neu zu besetzen
### Ihre Aufgaben ###
Aufgaben im gesamtbetrieblichen Kontext des Gemeindeverbandes
* Mitarbeit in der Geschäftsleitung des Zentrums für Soziales
* Aktive Mitarbeit an der Betriebsentwicklung und dem Qualitätsmanagement
* Externe Kommunikation des Fachbereichs in Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsführung
* Zielgerichtete, wirkungsvolle und nachhaltige Erledigung der übertragenen Aufgaben, insbesondere des politischen und betrieblichen Leistungsauftrages
* Mitwirkung in internen und externen Arbeitsgruppen, Projekten und Fachgremien
Aufgaben im Rahmen der Funktion Personalführung Der Fachbereich umfasst 47 Mitarbeitende. Ihnen direkt unterstellt sind die Teamleitungen der Sozialberatung und der Administration an beiden Standorten sowie die Teamleitung der Schulsozialarbeit.
* Personalführung, Förderung und Begleitung von Mitarbeitenden
* Sicherstellung von Qualität, Wissenstransfer und fachlicher Entwicklung
* Gestaltung von Abläufen, Prozessen und Konzepten
* Zusammenarbeit mit Gemeinden, Fachstellen, Behörden und weiteren Anspruchsgruppen
Aufgaben in der Klientenarbeit
* Beratung und Begleitung von Jugendlichen, Erwachsenen, Paaren und Familien in komplexen sozialen Fragestellungen
* Beratungen im Bereich der wirtschaftlichen und persönlichen Sozialhilfe
* Beratung in Fragen der Sozialversicherungen, Budget- und Einkommensverwaltung
### Das bringen Sie mit ###
* Bachelor oder Master in Sozialer Arbeit
* Mehrjährige Führungserfahrung im Sozialbereich
* Hohe Zuverlässigkeit und Belastbarkeit
* Konfliktfähigkeit und Durchsetzungsfähigkeit
* Kenntnisse im Controlling, Qualitätsmanagement und in der Betriebsentwicklung
* Integrative, reife und loyale Persönlichkeit

Bezahlte Pausen von 15 min. pro Halbtag 25-33 Tage Ferien, Möglichkeit zu unbezahltem Urlaub/Sabbatical und zusätzlichen Ferienkauf von 1-2 Wochen Wertschätzende Atmosphäre und kollegiales Arbeitsklima Flexibles Arbeitszeitmodell, Möglichkeit zu Homeoffice Frei am Geburtstag (pensenbezogen) Zeitlich sowie finanzielle Unterstützung bei Weiterbildungen

**Description de l'entreprise**
Le présent et le futur d-Audemars Piguet se construisent grâce à la contribution de tous nos talents. Inspirés par la richesse de notre passé, nous sommes enthousiastes à l-idée de ce que nous créerons dans le futur. Ensemble, nous sommes résolument tournés vers l-avenir et en quête continue d-excellence dans tous nos métiers.
Si notre mission vous inspire, venez forger votre propre chemin au sein de notre famille pour que l-on continue de créer l'extraordinaire. Écrivons le prochain chapitre de votre carrière ensemble !
**Description du poste**

Dans le cadre d-une création de poste, nous recherchons un Manager Services généraux chargé de piloter l-ensemble des activités liées aux bâtiments et infrastructures, à la santé, sécurité et sûreté au travail ainsi qu-au support informatique de 1er niveau du site.
Véritable partenaire des opérations, vous garantissez la disponibilité, la sécurité et la performance de ces domaines. Vous jouez un rôle clé dans la conduite de projets et l-amélioration continue de l-environnement de travail, en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires internes et externes.
Vous aurez la responsabilité de garantir la conformité réglementaire du site sur l'ensemble des domaines relatifs aux infrastructures, à la santé et sécurité au travail, à la protection incendie, à la sûreté, à l'environnement et aux obligations légales applicables.

**Management et leadership**
* Encadrer, animer et développer une équipe pluridisciplinaire.
* Favoriser un climat de travail positif, collaboratif et orienté résultats.
* Développer la cohésion d'équipe et accompagner les collaborateurs dans leur montée en compétences.
* Fédérer les différentes parties prenantes autour des objectifs communs.
**Services généraux, bâtiment et infrastructures**
* Assurer la gestion et le bon fonctionnement des bâtiments, installations et infrastructures des sites.
* Garantir la maintenance, l'entretien et l'évolution des équipements.
* Piloter les prestataires externes et veiller à la qualité des prestations fournies.
* Assurer la gestion des budgets liés à votre périmètre.
* Assurer la conformité réglementaire des installations, le suivi documentaire ainsi que la bonne réalisation des audits.
* Veiller au respect des exigences environnementales applicables et coordonner les actions nécessaires au maintien de la conformité du site.
**Informatique**
* Superviser les activités de support informatique de 1er niveau du site en collaboration avec les équipes concernées.
* Coordonner les activités de support informatique local en lien avec les équipes IT Groupe.
* Participer à la définition des besoins et à la mise en œuvre des évolutions technologiques.
**Santé, Sécurité au Travail (SST) et Sûreté**
* Assumer le rôle de référent SST du site
* Mettre en œuvre et maintenir le système de gestion SST
* Assurer la réalisation des analyses de risques, piloter les enquêtes d'accidents et garantir le suivi des mesures correctives
* Préparer les inspections SUVA et autorités
* Assurer la conformité réglementaire des installations et des pratiques.
* Promouvoir une culture sécurité forte auprès de l'ensemble des collaborateurs.
* Assurer le respect des exigences Incendies, coordonner les contrôles réglementaires et maintenir les dispositifs de protection incendie opérationnels.
**Gestion de projets**
* Piloter des projets d'infrastructure, de construction, de rénovation et d'amélioration des bâtiments.
* Coordonner les différents intervenants internes et externes.
* Garantir le respect des coûts, des délais et des standards de qualité.
* Être force de proposition dans l'amélioration continue des infrastructures et des services.
* Participer à la définition et au maintien des plans de continuité d'activité et de gestion des risques du site.

* Formation supérieure (Ingénieur, Master ou équivalent) dans un domaine technique, industriel ou lié aux infrastructures.
* Expérience confirmée de 10 ans minimum dans un environnement industriel, incluant une responsabilité significative en santé et sécurité au travail (SST), gestion des risques et conformité réglementaire.
* Expérience avérée dans le pilotage de services aux sites industriels ou de fonctions support à forte transversalité, couvrant tout ou partie des domaines suivants : infrastructures, services généraux, SST, sûreté ou facility management.
* Expérience réussie dans la responsabilité globale d'un ou plusieurs sites industriels, avec la coordination de plusieurs fonctions support et l'animation de réseaux d'experts internes et externes.
* Expérience confirmée dans le management d'équipes pluridisciplinaires ainsi que dans l'accompagnement et le développement des collaborateurs.
* Forte capacité à évoluer dans des environnements complexes et transversaux, à coordonner des métiers variés et à fédérer les parties prenantes autour d'objectifs communs.
* Solide expérience dans le pilotage de projets transverses, la gestion budgétaire et la conduite du changement au sein d'environnements exigeants.
* Bonne compréhension des enjeux liés à la continuité des activités, à la sûreté et à l'exploitation d'un site industriel.
* Leadership fédérateur, vision globale et capacité à prendre de la hauteur pour arbitrer des enjeux multiples et accompagner durablement la performance du site.

* Les assurances maladie (base et complémentaire)
